Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] (P2), and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be the assigned energy observable of a declared isolated system with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]), and write $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$. Then:

(a) **Energy law and moments.** For every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)E_H(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)E_H(B)\bigr)=\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ likewise $\|E_H(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_H(B)\psi\|^{2}$. If $\psi(0)\ne0$ and $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, the mean and second moment of the energy law of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ are finite and time-independent. For any nonzero representative $\psi(0)$ their time-zero values are
$$\frac{\langle H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0),\psi(0)\rangle}{\|\psi(0)\|^{2}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\frac{\|H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0)\|^{2}}{\|\psi(0)\|^{2}},$$
respectively. The displayed conservation of moments makes no assertion that these moments are finite for preparations outside this domain hypothesis.

(b) **Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable that is compatible with the energy ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)). Then its outcome law is time-independent: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B).$$

(c) **Stationary states are exactly the eigenrays.** Let $\psi\in H$, $\psi\ne0$. The pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, that is $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, if and only if $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$: $\psi\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. In that case $\psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi(0)$ for every $t$, and every assigned sharp observable has a time-independent outcome law in this preparation: $\mu^{A}_{[\psi(t)]}(B)=\mu^{A}_{[\psi(0)]}(B)$ for every $(A,u_A)$, every Borel $B$ and every $t$.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** No equilibration, relaxation, decay or convergence of the law of an arbitrary preparation is asserted; no moment beyond those finite at time zero is claimed; the converse of (b) — constancy of the law of a bounded observable in every preparation implying strong spectral compatibility with the energy — is not asserted for a general (possibly unbounded) $H_{\mathrm{op}}$; and the item is conditional on the isolated-system idealization of P4, asserting no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its
scalar law is the model's Born position law,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(d) for every unitary $V\in U(r)$, with $V_{\times}$ the matrix action of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clause (b),
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi},\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi};$$

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$. The real outcome spaces remain $\mathbb R$;
zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value
eigenstate. Finite-resolution records use the displayed Borel bin probabilities.

derivations.claim: [Energy observable and spectrum] By [F1], $H_{\kappa}$ is self-adjoint on the dense domain $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$; with the declared unit joule the pair $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [F4]. Write $c_{0}:=\hbar^{2}/2m>0$, so that $H_{\kappa}=c_{0}C_{\gamma}$. By [F3] applied to $A=C_{\gamma}$, $c_{0}A$ is self-adjoint and $\sigma(c_{0}A)=c_{0}\sigma(A)$, whence $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H_{\kappa})=c_{0}\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(C_{\gamma})=c_{0}[0,+\infty)=[0,+\infty)$. A point $\lambda\in\sigma(H_{\kappa})\cap(-\infty,0)$ has $\lambda/c_{0}\in\sigma(C_{\gamma})\cap(-\infty,0)$, so by [F2] it is an eigenvalue of $C_{\gamma}$ of finite multiplicity isolated in $\mathbb R$; by clause (d) of [F3] the eigenspaces correspond exactly under the scaling, so $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $H_{\kappa}$ of the same finite multiplicity, isolated because $c_{0}$ is a homeomorphism of $\mathbb R$, and the set of such $\lambda$ is at most countable as the image of an at-most-countable set. Boundedness below is [F2] together with the scaling, and the action formula is [F1]. This proves (a).

[Flow] By (a) and [F5] the family $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar)$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group; the Schroedinger equation holds in the norm-differentiable sense exactly for $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\kappa})$; density preparations evolve as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$. This is (b).

[Stationary states and readings] Let $\psi\ne0$. By [F5], $[\psi]$ is stationary exactly when $\psi\in D(H_{\kappa})$ and $H_{\kappa}\psi=E\psi$ for some $E\in\mathbb R$; then $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$ and every bounded assigned sharp observable has a time-independent outcome law. For a normalised such $\psi$ the energy law is given by [F4] as $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which equals $1$ for $B\ni E$ and $0$ otherwise, i.e. the point mass $\delta_{E}$. The position law is [F6], and the two readings of the same preparation are clause (d) of the statement.

[Spectral support and exact values] By clause (d) of [F4], $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\sigma(H_{\kappa}))=1$ for every preparation; by clause (c) of [F4] an exact value $\lambda$ has probability equal to the total weight of the eigenspace at $\lambda$ when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue, and zero otherwise. Claim (a) identifies the negative eigenvalues as the only spectral points asserted to be eigenvalues on this page, so the item makes no eigenvalue claim at $0$ or on the positive half-line; this is clause (e) with its recorded exclusions.

[Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give (a) and (b), steps 2.2 and 2.3 give (c)-(e); only the declared model, the framework postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and the cited mathematics were used, so the statement is conditional as recorded in (f), and no empirical identification or measured value is asserted.

boundaries.evidence: Statement(b) has a unitary family over every real time, with U(0)=I established in step 2.1. Empty Borel events in clauses (d)-(e) have zero spectral projection and zero outcome probability under F6. These events do not require a nonempty-event restriction.
Step 2.2 covers the value 0, the continuum threshold, and records that no eigenvalue claim is made there.
Step 1.1 fixes the parametrisation with a single mass parameter m and coupling kappa, and the scaling c_0=hbar^2/2m is strictly positive.
Step 1.1 records that every negative spectral point is an eigenvalue of finite multiplicity, which includes the possibility of repeated eigenvalues without claiming simplicity.
Step 1.1 computes the essential spectrum with the endpoint 0 and step 2.2 treats the exact-value reading at the threshold.
The proof uses the spectral theorem, Kato-Rellich and the essential-spectrum theorem under Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, declared and used in steps 1.1 and 2.2.
Step 2.1 proves the forward direction of the stationary-state criterion: an eigenvector gives a stationary preparation.
Step 2.1 invokes the cited stationary-state criterion, which is a biconditional between stationarity and the eigenvector equation, in the reverse direction as well.

risk_review.notes: Read all five proof steps and every declared supplier statement. Infinitesimal kinetic bound supplies the singular Coulomb operator on H2, rather than bounded-potential perturbation. Positive c0 preserves domains, eigenvectors and their multiplicities; resolvent scaling and eigen-space correspondence preserve isolated finite-multiplicity points and hence essential spectrum. Dynamics derivative is asserted exactly on domain; nonzero stationary rays are characterized in the cited theorem. PVM support and singleton masses are distinct; outside-spectrum energies have probability zero. No positive/zero eigenvalue classification is used here, no measured constants or detector model are assumed. Central Definition status repair needs no consumer edit.

citations.quote:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the framework data of clause (a) of the declared
central-potential model [[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]
with a declared mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, the state space
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the componentwise position and momentum
families and the action constant $\hbar>0$ of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared one-centre Coulomb model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, fix a real **coupling** $\kappa>0$ with the declared
unit $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and put
$$\gamma:=\frac{2m\kappa}{\hbar^{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{m^{-1}}),\qquad C_{\gamma}:=-\Delta-\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}\ \text{ on }\ D(C_{\gamma})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
the self-adjoint operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] clause (c). The **assigned
energy operator** of the one-centre Coulomb model is
$$H_{\kappa}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,C_{\gamma},$$
with domain $D(H_{\kappa}):=D(C_{\gamma})$; by
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] clauses (a)
and (b) it is self-adjoint with the same domain, and by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] together with
the action formula of the cited theorem it acts by
$$H_{\kappa}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f-\kappa\frac{f}{|\cdot|}\qquad(f\in D(H_{\kappa})),$$
where $\Delta_{w}$ is the weak Laplacian. The model declares the **length
scale** $a_{\kappa}:=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, read in metres, and the **energy
scale** $\mathcal E_{\kappa}:=m\kappa^{2}/(2\hbar^{2})=\hbar^{2}/(2ma_{\kappa}^{2})$,
read in joules. The model adopts $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ as its declared
energy observable for the one-centre problem; the self-adjointness is the
cited theorem's and no spectral property is presupposed here.

**(c) The declared radial reading of the one-centre model.** Let $U$ and
$(A_{l})_{l\ge0}$ be the unitary and the radial operators of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] clauses (a)-(d):
$U$ maps $H_{0}$ onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^{2}((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C)$ with
$UH_{\kappa}U^{*}=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{l}$, and each $A_{l}$ is self-adjoint
with form domain $V_{l}$ and domain $D(A_{l})$. The model declares the
**sector $(l,m)$ radial energy operator** $A_{l}^{(\kappa)}:=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{l}$,
read in joules, and, for a class $u\in D(A_{l})$, the **declared radial
equation** is the distributional identity
$$-u''(r)+\Bigl(\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}-\frac{\gamma}{r}\Bigr)u(r)=A_{l}u(r)\qquad\text{on }(0,\infty),$$
which by clause (c) of the cited theorem is an ordinary differential equation
with $C^{2}$ representative whenever $A_{l}u=Eu$ for a constant $E$. The
**regular reduced solution** at energy attribute $k>0$ is the function
$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$ of clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]], with $v$ the regular
power series of that clause; the pair uses it as the declared radial template
of the model, not as a physical state, until the normalisation and spectral
theorems of the page identify it.

**(d) The declared two-body Coulomb model.** As a further model assumption,
take two **distinguishable** spinless massive particles with declared mass
parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ (unit kg) and opposite declared charges: particle 1
carries charge $-q_{-}$ and particle 2 carries charge $+q_{+}$, where the
charge magnitudes $q_{-},q_{+}>0$ are read in coulombs. Declare the **pair
coupling**
$$\kappa:=\frac{q_{-}q_{+}}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}},\qquad \varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1},$$
where $\mu_{0}$ is the declared magnetic constant of the SI conventions and
$c$ the speed of light, both as in clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the identification
$\kappa=q_{-}q_{+}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ is a constitutive assumption of the
model, and $\kappa$ is read in $\mathrm{J\,m}$. Its equal-magnitude,
net-neutral submodel is $q_{-}=q_{+}=q>0$, with charges $-q,+q$ and
$\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$; this is the branch used by the later
relative-dipole consumers. The two-particle state space is the Hilbert tensor product of
two copies of the one-particle space of clause (a) as in
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], identified with
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$ through
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]; the spin-zero internal
factor is trivial, and because the two particles are of different species no
symmetrisation is imposed (the case of identical species belongs to the
identical-particle sector of P6 and is not used here). The **assigned energy
operator** is
$$H_{2}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{1}}\Delta_{x_{1}}-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{2}}\Delta_{x_{2}}-\frac{\kappa}{|x_{1}-x_{2}|},\qquad D(H_{2}):=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C),$$
which is self-adjoint by clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]]. Let
$$\Phi(x_{1},x_{2}):=(R,r),\qquad R:=\frac{m_{1}x_{1}+m_{2}x_{2}}{M},\quad r:=x_{1}-x_{2},\quad M:=m_{1}+m_{2},$$
be the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map of that theorem, with its
unitary $U_{\Phi}$. The model declares the **centre-of-mass/relative reading**
$U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ of clause (c) of
that theorem, with the **reduced mass**
$$\mu:=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{kg}),$$
the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2M}\Delta_{R}$
and the **relative operator** $C_{\mu}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu}\Delta_{r}-\frac{\kappa}{|r|}$;
the relative operator is exactly the one-centre Coulomb operator of clause
(b) with mass parameter $\mu$. The energy operators $H_{2}$, $T_{R}$ and
$C_{\mu}$ are each read in joules. The model further declares the **fixed-nucleus
reading**: the one-centre model of clauses (b), (c) with mass parameter $m_{1}$
is read as the limiting description in which the second particle is
infinitely heavy, $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$ at fixed $m_{1},\kappa$;
this is a declared limiting reading, and no convergence theorem for operators
or states is asserted by it.

**(e) The hydrogen-like identification.** A **hydrogen-like ion** assignment of
the two-body model is the choice $m_{1}=m_{\mathrm e}$ (electron mass
parameter), $m_{2}=m_{\mathrm n}$ (nuclear mass parameter), $q_{-}=e$ (the
elementary charge of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]) and $q_{+}=Ze$ (nuclear charge
magnitude), so that $\kappa=Ze^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ for a declared
positive integer $Z$. The **hydrogen assignment** is the specialization
$Z=1$, $m_{2}=m_{\mathrm p}$, for which $q_{-}=q_{+}=e$ and the pair is
net-neutral. These assignments use empirical mass and charge parameters; any
comparison of the model's consequences with a laboratory hydrogen atom is a
tested identification in the sense of clause (iii) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and carries the
uncertainty of that identification. The model declares no numerical value of
$m_{\mathrm e},m_{\mathrm n},e,\mu_{0}$ or $\hbar$; numerical evaluations, when
made, use their declared or measured values as explicitly qualified empirical
inputs.

**(f) Scope exclusions.** Until their own items introduce them, the Coulomb
and hydrogen models exclude: spin, magnetic moment couplings and
spin–statistics assignments beyond the trivial spin-zero factor; relativistic
corrections, in particular any fine-structure splitting of the degeneracy of
the gross-structure levels; finite nuclear size, nuclear recoil beyond the
two-body reduction of clause (d), and nuclear structure; QED corrections such
as vacuum polarisation and the Lamb shift, and hyperfine structure; shielding
and many-body modification of the $1/r$ potential; the radiation extension,
spontaneous emission, radiation reaction and any photon, transition-frequency
or line-intensity statement; external electromagnetic fields; and any
scattering, ionisation or continuum process, which belongs to the scattering
items of the quantum-mechanics track. The model asserts no empirical result
and fixes no measured quantity.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the declared one-centre
Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and coupling $\kappa>0$, its assigned energy
operator $H_{\kappa}$ on $D(H_{\kappa})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
assigned sharp-observable reading
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the flow and
preparation reading [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and
the spin-zero position law
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model:
$H_{\kappa}$ is densely defined, self-adjoint and bounded below on
$D(H_{\kappa})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, acts by
$H_{\kappa}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f-\kappa f/|\cdot|$, and
$$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H_{\kappa})=[0,+\infty);$$
every point of $\sigma(H_{\kappa})\cap(-\infty,0)$ is an eigenvalue of finite
multiplicity, isolated in $\mathbb R$, and the set of negative eigenvalues is
at most countable;

(b) *Flow.* The family $U(t):=\exp(-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar)$ is the model's
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group; the Schroedinger equation
$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\kappa}\psi(t)$ holds in the norm-differentiable
sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\kappa})$, and for other
vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not asserted; density
preparations evolve by $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with $\rho(t)$ a density
operator for every $t$;

(c) *Stationary states.* For $\psi\in H_{0}$, $\psi\ne0$, the pure preparation
$[\psi]$ is stationary, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for all $t$, if and only if
$\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$; in that case, with eigenvalue $E$,
one has $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$, the energy outcome law is the point
mass $\delta_{E}$ for a normalised $\psi$, and every bounded assigned sharp
observable compatible with the energy has a time-independent outcome law in
this preparation;

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit vector $\psi$ the position outcome law is
$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$; if $\psi$ is in addition a unit
eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$ with eigenvalue $E$, then the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ are readings of the same
preparation through the declared observables, with no joint-measurement claim;

(e) *Spectral support and exact values.* For every preparation $\rho$ one has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\sigma(H_{\kappa}))=1$, and an exact energy value
$\lambda$ has $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ unless $\lambda$ is an
eigenvalue, in which case the probability is the total weight of the
eigenspace; in particular no exact value in $\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(H_{\kappa})$
is admissible, and the item asserts neither that $0$ is an eigenvalue nor any
statement about eigenvalues in the positive half-line, which are excluded by
the following radial items;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. It asserts no eigenvalue list, no
degeneracy, no transition, radiation or line-intensity statement, no
identification of $\kappa$, $m$ or $\hbar$ with measured constants, and no
empirical result.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let $H_{0}$ be the free operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=3$, this $c$ and $b=0$:
$$H_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem.
Let $D^{2}_{j}$ denote the second weak partial derivative in the $j$-th
coordinate, defined componentwise on the locally integrable classes of
$\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]),
write $\Delta_{w}:=D^{2}_{1}+D^{2}_{2}+D^{2}_{3}$ for the weak Laplacian
(defined on the classes whose three second weak partial derivatives lie in
$L^{2}$), and let $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ as sets and
$$H_{0}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\Delta_{w}f\qquad\text{for every }f\in D(H_{0});$$
equivalently, $\mathcal F_{2}(H_{0}f)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$ and
$\mathcal F_{2}\bigl(-\tfrac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f\bigr)(\xi)=c|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$, and the two $L^{2}$ classes agree.

(b) For every real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$, the
operator $H_{0}+M_{V}$ of clause (c) of the cited theorem, with domain
$D(H_{0})$, coincides with the operator $f\mapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf$
on the same domain; in particular, for $E\in\mathbb R$ and
$\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ the eigenvalue equation
$(H_{0}+M_{V})\psi=E\psi$ is equivalent to the weak equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ elementwise in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$.

The statement identifies operators on the same domain; it asserts neither
smoothness of the classes in $W^{2,2}$ nor any physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, and for
every $l\ge0$ let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]]; let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c),
with essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$
([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-essential-spectrum]]), and let $U$ be the polar unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] (d). Then:

(a) if $k>0$ and $j:=\gamma/(2k)-l-1\notin\mathbb N_0$, then the regular solution $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] is not square-integrable on $(0,\infty)$, and $-k^2$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_l$;

(b) the negative eigenvalues of $A_l$ are exactly the numbers
$$-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2},\qquad n\ge l+1,$$
each with one-dimensional eigenspace spanned by the corresponding regular solution $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$; in particular every negative eigenvalue of $A_l$ is simple;

(c) the negative eigenvalues of $C$ are exactly the numbers $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ with $n\ge1$;

(d) every eigenfunction of $C$ with negative eigenvalue lies in the closed span of the transported regular solutions: if $C\psi=E\psi$ with $E<0$ and $U\psi=(u_{lm})$, then $E=-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ for some $n\ge1$, and each nonzero $u_{lm}$ is a scalar multiple of the regular solution of $A_l$ at that energy.

This exhausts the negative spectrum of $A_l$ and of $C$ by the terminating
Laguerre solutions; no claim is made here about completeness of these
eigenfunctions in the negative spectral subspace, about the multiplicity of
the levels of $C$, or about any physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma\ge0$, $l\ge0$,
and let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] with form domain
$V_l$. Fix $k_{\min}>0$ and let $K:=\{k\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Re}k\ge k_{\min},\ \operatorname{Im}k\ge0\}$.
Then:

(a) *regular solution.* With $c_0:=1$, $c_{-1}:=0$ and
$$c_n:=-\frac{\gamma c_{n-1}+k^2c_{n-2}}{n(n+2l+1)}\qquad(n\ge1),$$
the series $\varphi_l(k,r):=r^{l+1}\sum_{n\ge0}c_nr^n$ converges for every $r>0$ and every $k\in\mathbb C$, the function $(k,r)\mapsto\varphi_l(k,r)$ is holomorphic in $k$ and $C^\infty$ in $r>0$, and $\varphi_l$ solves $-u''+\bigl(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r\bigr)u=k^2u$ with $\varphi_l(k,r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ as $r\downarrow0$;

(b) *Jost-type solution.* Put $a:=\gamma/(2k)$, $\theta(r):=kr+a\log r$, $w(r):=e^{i\theta(r)}$, $b:=a^2+l(l+1)+ia$ and consider the integral equation
$$v(r)=1+\int_r^\infty\frac{b}{s^2}\,w(s)^2\Bigl(\int_r^sw(y)^{-2}dy\Bigr)v(s)\,ds .$$
For every $k\in K$ with $k\ne0$ the equation has exactly one bounded solution $v(\cdot;k)$ on $[r_0,\infty)$ for some $r_0>0$ depending on $k$, and $v(r)=1+O(1/r)$, $v'(r)=O(1/r)$; the functions $f_l(k,r):=w(r)v(r)$ and $v$ are continuous on $K$, holomorphic in $k$ for $\operatorname{Im}k>0$, satisfy the radial equation $-\partial_r^2f_l+\bigl(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r\bigr)f_l=k^2f_l$ exactly, and obey the asymptotics
$$f_l=e^{i(kr+a\log r)}(1+O(1/r)),\qquad f_l'=e^{i(kr+a\log r)}[ik+O(1/r)]\qquad(r\to\infty);$$

(c) *Wronskians.* For real $k>0$ one has $W(\overline{f_l},f_l)=2ik$ and $W_l(k):=W(\varphi_l,f_l)\ne0$; consequently every solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ is $Af_l+B\overline{f_l}$ with $A,B\in\mathbb C$, and $\varphi_l$ is a nonzero complex multiple combination of $f_l,\overline{f_l}$;

(d) *no positive eigenvalue.* For real $k>0$ and $A,B\in\mathbb C$, if $g=Af_l+B\overline{f_l}$ then $\int_R^L|g(r)|^2dr=(|A|^2+|B|^2)[L-R-\gamma\log(L/R)/(2k^2)]+O(1)$ as $L\to\infty$ with $R>r_0$ fixed; hence $g\in L^2(r_0,\infty)$ if and only if $A=B=0$, and $k^2>0$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_l$.

All assertions concern the ordinary differential equation and the operator
$A_l$; no scattering amplitude, cross-section or physical interpretation is
asserted or computed.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma\ge0$, $l\ge0$,
let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] with spectral
measure $E_{A_l}$, and for $k>0$ let $\varphi_l(k,\cdot)$ and $f_l(k,\cdot)$
be the solutions of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-jost-volterra-solution]], with
$W_l(k):=W(\varphi_l(k,\cdot),f_l(k,\cdot))\ne0$. Write
$$\rho_l(E):=\frac{\sqrt E}{\pi\,|W_l(\sqrt E)|^2}\qquad(E>0).$$

For $g\in L^2(0,\infty)$ write $\mu_g(B):=\langle E_{A_l}(B)g,g\rangle$
for its finite positive scalar spectral measure, where $B\subseteq\mathbb R$
is Borel ([[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). A finite
positive Borel measure $\mu$ is *absolutely continuous* with respect to
Lebesgue measure $dE$ if $\mu(N)=0$ for every Borel set $N$ of Lebesgue measure
zero; it is *singular continuous* if it is carried by a Borel Lebesgue-null
set and has no atoms, meaning $\mu(\{E\})=0$ for every $E\in\mathbb R$.
Define the absolutely continuous subspace
$$\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A_l):=\{g\in L^2(0,\infty):\mu_g\text{ is absolutely continuous with respect to }dE\}.$$
It is a closed linear subspace because it equals
$\bigcap_{N:\,|N|=0}\ker E_{A_l}(N)$, where the intersection is over Borel
Lebesgue-null sets and $\mu_g(N)=\|E_{A_l}(N)g\|^2$.
For $I=(0,\infty)$, put
$$\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A_l;I):=\{g\in E_{A_l}(I)L^2(0,\infty):\mu_g\text{ is singular continuous}\}.$$
The set $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A_l;I)$ is a closed linear subspace:
linear combinations of such vectors have scalar measures supported on the
union of their null carriers and have no atoms, and these two properties pass
to limits of vectors by continuity of the PVM projections. Here $E_{A_l}(I)L^2$ is
*purely absolutely continuous* when it is contained in $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A_l)$,
and “$A_l$ has no singular-continuous spectrum on $I$” means
$\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A_l;I)=\{0\}$. Thus each operator spectral-type
phrase in (d) is a statement about the scalar PVM measures, not an additional
pointwise classification of energies.

Then:

(a) *resolvent kernel.* For $z=k^2$ with $\operatorname{Im}k>0$ and $k$ in the domain of the Jost construction, and for every $g\in L^2(0,\infty)$ with compact support, the resolvent is given by
$$((A_l-z)^{-1}g)(r)=\int_0^\infty G_l(r,s)g(s)\,ds,\qquad G_l(r,s):=-\frac{\varphi_l(k,\min(r,s))\,f_l(k,\max(r,s))}{W_l(k)},$$
and $G_l$ solves $(A_l-z)G_l=\delta$ in the sense that $-G''+(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r)G-zG=0$ away from $r=s$ and the derivative of $G$ has the jump $-1$ at $r=s$; moreover $\|(A_l-z)^{-1}\|\le1/|\operatorname{Im}z|$;

(b) *boundary value.* For real $k>0$ one has $\varphi_l(k,\cdot)$ real and, for all $r,s>0$,
$$\operatorname{Im}G_l(k^2+i0;r,s)=\frac{k\,\varphi_l(k,r)\varphi_l(k,s)}{|W_l(k)|^2};$$

(c) *spectral density.* For every $g\in L^2(0,\infty)$ and every $0<a<b$,
$$\langle E_{A_l}((a,b))g,g\rangle=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\frac1\pi\int_a^b\operatorname{Im}\bigl\langle(A_l-E-i\varepsilon)^{-1}g,g\bigr\rangle dE,$$
and if $g$ has compact support then
$$\langle E_{A_l}((a,b))g,g\rangle=\int_a^b\rho_l(E)\Bigl|\int_0^\infty\varphi_l(\sqrt E,r)g(r)\,dr\Bigr|^2dE;$$
consequently for compactly supported $g$ the measure $E_{A_l,g}(B):=\langle E_{A_l}(B)g,g\rangle$ restricted to $(0,\infty)$ is absolutely continuous with density $\rho_l(E)|\int\varphi_l g|^2$;

(d) *absolutely continuous spectrum; no zero eigenvalue.* For every $g\in L^2(0,\infty)$ the measure $E_{A_l,g}$ has no atom in $(0,\infty)$; the positive spectral subspace $E_{A_l}((0,\infty))L^2(0,\infty)$ is purely absolutely continuous and is the closed span of the positive spectral projections of compactly supported functions; it equals the absolutely continuous subspace of $A_l$, and $A_l$ has no singular continuous spectrum on $(0,\infty)$; moreover $0$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_l$.

No scattering phase, normalization of the continuum functions as a unitary
transform, or physical cross-section is asserted; the transform itself is the
subject of the companion item [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-onto-radial-continuum-transform]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$ and let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$. For $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$ and
$-l\le m\le l$ let $u_{nl}$ be the regular solution of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] at $k=\gamma/(2n)$
(the polynomial-exponential solution, unique up to a nonzero scalar), and put
$$\psi_{nlm}(x):=\frac{u_{nl}(r)}{r}Y_{lm}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega).$$
Then:

(a) each $\psi_{nlm}$ lies in $D(C)$ and $C\psi_{nlm}=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2}\psi_{nlm}$; the vectors $\psi_{nlm}$ with distinct labels are pairwise orthogonal, and for fixed $n$ the eigenspace of $C$ at $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ is exactly their span; it has dimension $\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^2$;

(b) after normalization, the family $(\psi_{nlm}/\|u_{nl}\|_2)_{n\ge1,0\le l\le n-1,-l\le m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal family of the negative spectral subspace $E_C((-\infty,0))L^2(\mathbb R^3)$;

(c) the family is not complete in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$: the nonnegative spectral subspace $E_C([0,\infty))L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ is nonzero (indeed infinite dimensional), so the bound states alone do not span $L^2$.

All claims concern the mathematical spectral decomposition of $C$; no physical
interpretation is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$H_0=-\Delta$ with $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the free operator
of [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
let $M$ be the multiplier $Mu=u/|\cdot|$ of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]], and let
$$C:=H_0-\gamma M,\qquad D(C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C),$$
be the self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c).
Write $\sigma_{\mathrm d}$, $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}$, $E$ for the discrete
spectrum, essential spectrum and spectral projection valued measure of
[[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]] and
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. Then:

(a) $C$ is bounded below and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(C)=[0,+\infty)$;

(b) every point of $\sigma(C)\cap(-\infty,0)$ lies in $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(C)$: it is an eigenvalue of $C$ of finite multiplicity isolated in $\mathbb R$, and the set of such eigenvalues is at most countable;

(c) the negative spectral subspace $E((-\infty,0))L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ is the closed linear span of the eigenspaces of $C$ for its negative eigenvalues.

No claim is made about the multiplicity or the number of the negative
eigenvalues, about the nonnegative part of the spectrum beyond
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(C)=[0,\infty)$, or about any physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma\ge0$, let
$C:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c) when $\gamma>0$, and the free Fourier multiplier when $\gamma=0$,
and let $U$ be the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] from $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$
onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^2\bigl((0,\infty),dr\bigr)$, with coefficients
$u_{lm}=r\,c_{lm}$. For $l\ge0$ let $V_l$ be the closure of
$C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$ in $L^2(0,\infty;\mathbb C)$ for the norm
$$\|u\|_{V_l}^2:=\int_0^\infty\Bigl(\Bigl|u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr|^2+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}|u(r)|^2+|u(r)|^2\Bigr)dr,$$
realized as the space of $u\in L^2$ with $u'-\frac ur\in L^2$ and
$\int|u|^2/r^2<\infty$ in the distributional sense
([[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and define
$$a_l(u,v):=\int_0^\infty\Bigl[\overline{\Bigl(v'(r)-\frac{v(r)}{r}\Bigr)}\Bigl(u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}u(r)\overline{v(r)}-\frac{\gamma}{r}u(r)\overline{v(r)}\Bigr]dr .$$
Then:

(a) $V_l$ is a dense linear subspace of $L^2(0,\infty)$ that is a Hilbert space for $\|\cdot\|_{V_l}$, the inclusion $V_l\hookrightarrow L^2(0,\infty)$ is continuous, and $a_l$ is a bounded symmetric sesquilinear form on $V_l$ that is closed and semibounded below;

(b) the operator $A_l$ defined by
$$D(A_l):=\Bigl\{u\in V_l:\exists\,f\in L^2(0,\infty)\ \text{with}\ a_l(u,v)=\langle f,v\rangle\ \forall v\in V_l\Bigr\},\qquad A_lu:=f,$$
is well defined, self-adjoint and bounded below; $D(A_l)$ is dense in $V_l$ in the norm $\|\cdot\|_{V_l}$ and $a_l(u,u)=\langle A_lu,u\rangle$ for $u\in D(A_l)$;

(c) for every $u\in D(A_l)$ the distributional identity $-u''+\bigl(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r\bigr)u=A_lu$ holds on $(0,\infty)$; consequently $u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty)$, $u$ is of class $C^1$ with $u'$ locally absolutely continuous, and the identity holds pointwise almost everywhere on $(0,\infty)$; if moreover $A_lu=Eu$ for some constant $E\in\mathbb C$ (in particular if $u$ is an eigenfunction of $A_l$), then $u$ is of class $C^2$ on $(0,\infty)$ and the differential equation holds pointwise there;

(d) *block identity.* For $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ with $U\psi=(u_{lm})$ one has $\psi\in D(C)$ if and only if $u_{lm}\in D(A_l)$ for every $(l,m)$ and $\sum_{l,m}\bigl(\|u_{lm}\|^2+\|A_lu_{lm}\|^2\bigr)<\infty$; then $U(C\psi)=(A_lu_{lm})_{l,m}$. Equivalently $UCU^*=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}A_l$ on $K$;

(e) *eigenfunction transport.* If $u\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu=Eu$ for some $E\in\mathbb R$, then the function $\psi(x):=u(r)Y_{l0}(\Omega)/r$ (with $x=r\Omega$) lies in $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, satisfies $C\psi=E\psi$, and $r\mapsto u(r)/r$ is bounded on $(0,1]$; moreover $\psi$ is bounded and continuous on $\mathbb R^3$.

No endpoint boundary condition is imposed by hand: the domain $D(A_l)$ is the
form-domain realization transported from $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and no
physical interpretation of $A_l$, $C$, $U$ or $\gamma$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$, let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), and let
$(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
$L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]. Write
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with Lebesgue measure and inner product linear
in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and let
$$K:=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^2\bigl((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C\bigr)$$
be the Hilbert direct sum over $l\ge0$, $-l\le m\le l$. For $\psi\in L^2$ and
each $(l,m)$ define the coefficient function and the reduced function
$$c_{lm}(r):=\int_{S^2}\psi(r\Omega)\overline{Y_{lm}(\Omega)}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\quad(r>0,\ \text{a.e.}),\qquad u_{lm}(r):=r\,c_{lm}(r).$$
Then:

(a) for every $\psi\in L^2$ and every $(l,m)$ the function $u_{lm}$ is a well-defined element of $L^2((0,\infty),dr)$ depending only on the class of $\psi$, and $U\psi:=(u_{lm})_{l,m}$ is a linear isometry of $L^2$ into (indeed onto) $K$ with
$$\|U\psi\|_K^2=\sum_{l\ge0}\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\int_0^\infty|u_{lm}(r)|^2\,dr=\|\psi\|_{L^2}^2;$$

(b) $U$ is unitary, and for every $(u_{lm})\in K$ the finite-subset sums $\sum_{l\le N,\,|m|\le l}u_{lm}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ converge in $L^2$ to a function $\psi$ with $U\psi=(u_{lm})$;

(c) on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ every $f\in C^2$ satisfies, in the notation $\partial_r f$, $\Delta_{S^2}f$ of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]],
$$\Delta f=\partial_r^2f+\frac2r\partial_rf+\frac1{r^2}\Delta_{S^2}f;$$

(d) for every $l\ge0$, $m$, and $u\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, the function $\psi:=u(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})\subseteq H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, its image under $U$ is the finite-support vector with $(l,m)$-entry $u$, and
$$-\Delta\psi=\frac1r\Bigl(-u''(r)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}u(r)\Bigr)Y_{lm}(\Omega),\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^3}|\nabla\psi|^2\,dx=\int_0^\infty\Bigl(\Bigl|u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr|^2+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}|u(r)|^2\Bigr)dr .$$

All statements are purely mathematical assertions about $L^2$ spaces, the
surface measure and the Laplacian; no physical interpretation and no statement
about operators with unbounded potentials is included.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a
densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $c>0$ be
real. Write $cA$ for the operator with domain $D(cA):=D(A)$ and
$(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$. Then:

(a) $cA$ is self-adjoint.

(b) For every $z\in\mathbb C$ one has $z\in\rho(cA)$ if and only if
$z/c\in\rho(A)$, and then
$(cA-z)^{-1}=c^{-1}(A-z/c)^{-1}$; consequently
$\rho(cA)=c\,\rho(A)$ and $\sigma(cA)=c\,\sigma(A)$.

(c) If some, hence every, resolvent of $A$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]), then every resolvent of $cA$ is compact and
$A$ and $cA$ have the same complete orthonormal eigenfamily $(e_j)_{j\in J}$.
If $N:=\dim H<\infty$, take $J=\{1,\ldots,N\}$; if $H$ is infinite dimensional,
take $J=\mathbb N$, with $|\mu_j|\to\infty$ and each eigenvalue repeated
according to its finite multiplicity. In both cases $Ae_j=\mu_je_j$,
$(cA)e_j=c\mu_je_j$, and
$$\sigma(A)=\{\mu_j:j\in J\},\qquad\sigma(cA)=\{c\mu_j:j\in J\}$$
with no other spectral points. The finite-dimensional conclusion also holds
without a separate compactness assumption, since bounded operators on such
$H$ are compact.

(d) Eigenvectors correspond exactly: for $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in H$,
$x\ne0$, one has $x\in D(A)$ and $Ax=\lambda x$ if and only if
$x\in D(cA)$ and $(cA)x=(c\lambda)x$; and every eigenvalue of $cA$ has the same
eigenspace as the corresponding eigenvalue of $A$.

(e) If $A\ge\gamma$ in the quadratic-form sense, meaning that
$\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge\gamma\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in D(A)$, then
$cA\ge c\gamma$ in the same sense.

Only the scaling of the given operator is asserted; no domain, spectrum or
eigenvector is claimed for any other rescaling, and no physical
interpretation is attached.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space, let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a densely defined
self-adjoint operator with spectral projection valued measure $E$ on the Borel
$\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $c>0$. Write $cA$ for the operator
with $D(cA):=D(A)$ and $(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$, and for $m_{c}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
$m_{c}(\lambda):=c\lambda$, define
$$F(B):=E\bigl(m_{c}^{-1}(B)\bigr)=E\bigl(c^{-1}B\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}).$$
Then:

(a) $F$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb R$;

(b) for every bounded Borel $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ the bounded integrals
satisfy $\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f\circ m_{c})$, and the operator
$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)$ of the spectral theorem equals $cA$ with
domain $D(A)$;

(c) consequently $F$ is the spectral projection valued measure $E_{cA}$ of
$cA$: for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$E_{cA}(B)=E\bigl(c^{-1}B\bigr);$$in particular the negative spectral subspaces agree,$$E_{cA}\bigl((-\infty,0)\bigr)H=E\bigl((-\infty,0)\bigr)H .$$

The assertion transfers the spectral measure along positive scaling of the
operator. It asserts no spectral type of a particular operator, no multiplicity
statement and no physical interpretation; $c<0$ is not covered, and no
statement is made about unbounded Borel functions of $cA$ beyond the identity
functional calculus stated in (b).

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $E_{A,x}(B):=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ be its scalar measures ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ say that $\lambda$ is an **eigenvalue** of $A$ when $Ax=\lambda x$ for some nonzero $x\in D(A)$, the domain-restricted reading of [[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]. Then:

(a) The orthogonal projection $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection of $H$ onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)=\{x\in D(A):Ax=\lambda x\}$; in particular $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$.

(b) For every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, that is every self-adjoint positive trace-class $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)), the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(\{\lambda\}))$ is the weight that the scalar law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ assigns to the singleton $\{\lambda\}$: it vanishes for every $\rho$ whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and it equals $1$ for the pure state $T_{u,u}$ of every unit eigenvector $u\in\ker(A-\lambda)$.

(c) If $A$ has no eigenvalues at all, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every density operator $\rho$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$: the scalar law of every state carries no point mass, while its values on general Borel sets remain $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$.

Clauses (a)-(c) are mathematical statements about $A$, $E_A$ and the density operators; no physical interpretation of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is asserted here.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its
scalar law is the model's Born position law,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(d) for every unitary $V\in U(r)$, with $V_{\times}$ the matrix action of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clause (b),
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi},\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi};$$

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$. The real outcome spaces remain $\mathbb R$;
zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value
eigenstate. Finite-resolution records use the displayed Borel bin probabilities.

derivations.claim: [Eigenpairs and degeneracy] By [F3] clause (a), $\psi_{nlm}\in D(C_{\gamma})$ and $C_{\gamma}\psi_{nlm}=-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4n^{2}}\psi_{nlm}$; by [F5] the eigenpair correspondence gives $\psi_{nlm}\in D(H_{\kappa})$ and $H_{\kappa}\psi_{nlm}=c_{0}\bigl(-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4n^{2}}\bigr)\psi_{nlm}$. With $c_{0}=\hbar^{2}/2m$ and $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$ one computes $c_{0}\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\cdot\frac{4m^{2}\kappa^{2}}{4\hbar^{4}}=\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}$, so $H_{\kappa}\psi_{nlm}=E_{n}\psi_{nlm}$ with $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$; the identity $E_{n}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}$ follows from $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$. Normalising preserves the eigenpair relation and orthogonality is inherited from [F3] clause (b); the eigenspace of $C_{\gamma}$ at $-\gamma^{2}/(4n^{2})$ is exactly the span of the $\psi_{nlm}$ with the stated labels, of dimension $n^{2}$, and by [F5] the eigenspaces of $H_{\kappa}$ at $E_{n}$ are the same, so the $\Psi_{nlm}$ of fixed $n$ span exactly that eigenspace. This proves (a) and the eigenspace claim of (b).

[Completeness in the negative subspace] By [F3] clause (b) the family $(\Psi_{nlm})$ is a complete orthonormal family of $E_{C_{\gamma}}((-\infty,0))L^{2}$; by [F5] the spectral projections satisfy $E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))=E_{C_{\gamma}}(c_{0}^{-1}(-\infty,0))=E_{C_{\gamma}}((-\infty,0))$, so the same family is a complete orthonormal family of $E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))L^{2}$. This is (c).

[No nonnegative eigenvalue] Suppose $H_{\kappa}\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\psi\ne0$ and $\lambda\ge0$; by [F5] this is equivalent to $C_{\gamma}\psi=(\lambda/c_{0})\psi$ with $\lambda/c_{0}\ge0$, and $\psi\in D(C_{\gamma})$. Write $U\psi=(u_{lm})$; by the block identity [F4] one has $U\psi\in D(\bigoplus_{(l,m)}A_{l})$ and $(A_{l}u_{lm})_{l,m}=U C_{\gamma}U^{*}U\psi=(\lambda/c_{0})U\psi$, so $A_{l}u_{lm}=(\lambda/c_{0})u_{lm}$ for every $(l,m)$. Since $U$ is unitary and $\psi\ne0$, some component $u_{l_{0}m_{0}}$ is nonzero, and $\lambda/c_{0}\ge0$ is an eigenvalue of $A_{l_{0}}$, contradicting [F2] (no eigenvalue $k^{2}>0$, and no eigenvalue $0$). Hence every eigenvalue of $H_{\kappa}$ is negative; by [F2] clauses (b) and (d) together with [F5] the negative eigenvalues of $H_{\kappa}$ are exactly the numbers $c_{0}\,(-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4n^{2}})=-\frac{\gamma^{2}c_{0}}{4n^{2}}$, $n\ge1$, with the eigenspaces of step 1.1. This completes (b).

[Non-exhaustion and the continuum] By [F3] clause (c) the nonnegative spectral subspace of $C_{\gamma}$ is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional; by [F5] at $B=[0,+\infty)$, $E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))=E_{C_{\gamma}}([0,+\infty))$, so the nonnegative spectral subspace of $H_{\kappa}$ is nonzero and infinite dimensional, and by step 1.2 the closed span of the bound states, namely the negative spectral subspace, is a proper subspace of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$; this is the non-completeness in (d). For a unit vector $\psi$ in the nonnegative subspace the outcome law obeys $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ by [F6], and for Borel $B\subseteq(-\infty,0)$ the multiplicativity in [F5] with $B\cap[0,+\infty)=\varnothing$ gives $E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)\psi=E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))\psi=E_{H_{\kappa}}(\varnothing)\psi=0$, so strictly negative energy outcomes have probability zero.

[Energy-law reading] For a unit $\psi$, [F6] gives the sigma-additive law $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}$ with $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)\psi\|^{2}$; its restriction to $(-\infty,0)$ is carried by the eigenvalues $E_{n}$ by step 1.1 and step 2.1, and [F6]'s atom rule gives $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(\{E_{n}\})=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(\{E_{n}\})\psi\|^{2}=w_{n}$, so additivity gives $\sum_{n}w_{n}=\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}((-\infty,0))=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))\psi\|^{2}\le1$. For $\psi=\Psi_{nlm}$ step 1.1 gives $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}=\delta_{E_{n}}$. This is (e).

[Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give (a) and (b), step 1.2 gives (c), step 2.2 gives (d) and step 3.1 gives (e); only the declared model, P1, P2, P4, P5 and the cited mathematics were used, so no measured line, transition rate, photon coupling or empirical result is asserted, and the absolute continuity of the positive spectral subspace is not claimed for the scaled model. This completes the proof with the recorded scope (f).

boundaries.evidence: The fixed level labels include n=1,l=m=0. Statement(e) admits empty Borel subsets and a state with zero negative spectral weight; step 3.1 assigns zero to those events and weights by the projection law and additivity. It does not require bound support in every preparation.
Step 2.1 treats the value 0 in the eigenvalues-by-exhaustion reading and the nonnegative half-line in step 2.2, where no eigenvalue lies at 0.
Step 1.1 covers n=1, where the level carries one state and E_1 is the ground energy; the degeneracy count 1^2=1 is included.
Steps 1.1 and 1.2 compute the model degeneracy n^2 of each level and prove that the eigenspace has exactly that dimension.
Step 2.2 treats the endpoint 0 of the negative half-line and the threshold reading of the continuum, and records that the nonnegative subspace is infinite dimensional.
The proof uses the Coulomb spectral suppliers and the spectral theorem under Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, declared and used in steps 1.1-2.2.
Step 1.2 proves that every eigenvalue of H_kappa is one of the E_n, using the block identity and the absence of nonnegative eigenvalues of the radial operators.
Step 1.1 proves that each E_n is an eigenvalue with the stated eigenvector, which is the reverse reading of the exhaustion claim.

risk_review.notes: Read every step and exact negative-subspace, radial endpoint, Laguerre exhaustion, Jost positive-eigenvalue exclusion, continuum zero-eigenvalue exclusion, scaling-PVM and atom statements. c0*gamma²/4=m*kappa²/(2*hbar²); n=1 has l=m=0, degeneracy one; sum(2l+1)=n². Unit scaling preserves orthogonality and eigenspaces. A nonzero direct-sum vector has a nonzero component, ruling out both zero and positive eigenvalues by separate supplier clauses. Negative-subspace completeness follows from F3 and the PVM scaling identity, not completeness on all L2; positive subspace is infinite dimensional. Negative weights sum to at most one. AC/AComega and physical model scope retained. No empirical data used.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$ and let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$. For $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$ and
$-l\le m\le l$ let $u_{nl}$ be the regular solution of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] at $k=\gamma/(2n)$
(the polynomial-exponential solution, unique up to a nonzero scalar), and put
$$\psi_{nlm}(x):=\frac{u_{nl}(r)}{r}Y_{lm}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega).$$
Then:

(a) each $\psi_{nlm}$ lies in $D(C)$ and $C\psi_{nlm}=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2}\psi_{nlm}$; the vectors $\psi_{nlm}$ with distinct labels are pairwise orthogonal, and for fixed $n$ the eigenspace of $C$ at $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ is exactly their span; it has dimension $\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^2$;

(b) after normalization, the family $(\psi_{nlm}/\|u_{nl}\|_2)_{n\ge1,0\le l\le n-1,-l\le m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal family of the negative spectral subspace $E_C((-\infty,0))L^2(\mathbb R^3)$;

(c) the family is not complete in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$: the nonnegative spectral subspace $E_C([0,\infty))L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ is nonzero (indeed infinite dimensional), so the bound states alone do not span $L^2$.

All claims concern the mathematical spectral decomposition of $C$; no physical
interpretation is asserted.

Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the readings of the
declared one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and coupling $\kappa>0$, its assigned energy
operator $H_{\kappa}$ with length scale $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, and
the energy-observable content of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$, $-l\le m\le l$ let
$\psi_{nlm}$ be the regular bound solutions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] and put
$\Psi_{nlm}:=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$, and put
$$E_{n}:=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}\qquad(n\ge1).$$
Then:

(a) for every label, $\Psi_{nlm}\in D(H_{\kappa})$, $\|\Psi_{nlm}\|=1$,
$H_{\kappa}\Psi_{nlm}=E_{n}\Psi_{nlm}$, and vectors with distinct labels are
orthogonal; the vectors $\Psi_{nlm}$ of fixed $n$ span a subspace of dimension
$\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^{2}$;

(b) the eigenvalues of $H_{\kappa}$ are exactly the numbers $E_{n}$, $n\ge1$;
the eigenspace of $H_{\kappa}$ at $E_{n}$ is exactly
$\operatorname{span}\{\Psi_{nlm}:0\le l\le n-1,\ -l\le m\le l\}$, so the model
assigns to the level $n$ the **model degeneracy** $n^{2}$; in particular
$H_{\kappa}$ has no eigenvalues in $[0,+\infty)$, whose spectral content is
entirely essential spectrum $[0,+\infty)$ in the sense of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] (a);

(c) the family
$(\Psi_{nlm})_{n\ge1,\,0\le l\le n-1,\,-l\le m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal
family of the negative spectral subspace
$E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the bound states
span exactly the preparations whose energy outcomes are negative almost surely;

(d) the family is not complete in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the
nonnegative spectral subspace $E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional, and every unit vector $\psi$ in it has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=0$ for every Borel $B\subseteq(-\infty,0)$, i.e.
strictly negative energy outcomes have probability zero in such a preparation;
consequently the bound states of the model do not exhaust its state space and
the model possesses continuum states which are not bound states;

(e) *Energy-law reading.* For every unit vector $\psi$ the restriction of the
energy outcome law to the negative half-line is the discrete law
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}\delta_{E_{n}}$ with weights
$w_{n}:=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(\{E_{n}\})\psi\|^{2}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))\psi\|^{2}\le1$; for
$\psi=\Psi_{nlm}$ the whole law is the point mass $\delta_{E_{n}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The values $E_{n}$ are model
parameters determined by $\hbar,m,\kappa$; no numerical value, no measured
line, no transition rate, no photon or light-matter coupling and no empirical
result is asserted. The absolute continuity of the positive spectral subspace
is recorded by the cited mathematics for the unscaled operator and is not
restated for the scaled model here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, $l\ge0$,
$k>0$, let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]], write
$$j:=\frac{\gamma}{2k}-l-1,$$
and for $a=2l+1$ and $n\in\mathbb N_0$ let
$$L_n^{(a)}(x):=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i\binom{n+a}{n-i}\frac{x^i}{i!}$$
be the $n$-th Laguerre polynomial of order $a$. Then:

(a) *substitution.* A $C^2$ function $u$ on $(0,\infty)$ satisfies $-u''+(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r)u=-k^2u$ if and only if $v(x):=e^{x/2}x^{-(l+1)}u(x/2k)$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $(0,\infty)$;

(b) *regular series.* With $v_0:=1$ and
$$v_{i+1}:=\frac{(i-j)v_i}{(i+1)(i+2l+2)}\qquad(i\ge0),$$
the power series $v(x):=\sum_{i\ge0}v_ix^i$ converges for every $x\in\mathbb R$ and defines a solution of $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) *regular solution and general solution.* The function
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r):=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$$
