$$\gamma:=\frac{2m\kappa}{\hbar^{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{m^{-1}}),\qquad C_{\gamma}:=-\Delta-\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}\ \text{ on }\ D(C_{\gamma})=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$

$$H_{\kappa}:=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,C_{\gamma},$$
with domain $D(H_{\kappa}):=D(C_{\gamma})$; by
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] clauses (a)
and (b) it is self-adjoint with the same domain, and by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] together with

**(c) The declared radial reading of the one-centre model.** Let $U$ and

$$-u''(r)+\Bigl(\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}-\frac{\gamma}{r}\Bigr)u(r)=A_{l}u(r)\qquad\text{on }(0,\infty),$$
which by clause (c) of the cited theorem is an ordinary differential equation

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: $j$ has dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$; it is a probability flux, not a charge flux.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

derivations.claim: [Length-scale identity] By definition $a_{\kappa}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{m\kappa}$, so $a_{\kappa}^{2}=\frac{\hbar^{4}}{m^{2}\kappa^{2}}$ and $\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\cdot\frac{m^{2}\kappa^{2}}{\hbar^{4}}=\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}$; multiplying by $n^{-2}$ gives the equality of the two expressions for $E_{n}$ in (a), and $n=1$ gives $E_{1}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}}$.

[Fine-structure parametrisation] By definition $\alpha=\frac{\kappa}{\hbar c}$, hence $\kappa=\alpha\hbar c$ and $\kappa^{2}=\alpha^{2}\hbar^{2}c^{2}$; substituting into $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ gives $E_{n}=-\frac{m\alpha^{2}c^{2}}{2n^{2}}$, and substituting into $a_{\kappa}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{m\kappa}$ gives $a_{\kappa}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{m\alpha\hbar c}=\frac{\hbar}{m\alpha c}$; this is (b).

[Reduced-mass factor] By [L2], $\mathcal E_{n}=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$ and $\mu=\frac{m_{1}}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}$, so $\mu=\frac{\mu}{m_{1}}\cdot m_{1}$ gives $\mathcal E_{n}=\frac{\mu}{m_{1}}\bigl(-\frac{m_{1}\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}\bigr)$, where the bracket is the fixed-nucleus energy of the one-centre model with mass parameter $m_{1}$; since $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ one has $0<\frac{1}{1+m_{1}/m_{2}}<1$, so the relative binding magnitudes are strictly smaller than the fixed-nucleus ones. This is (c).

[Dimensions] Using [L3]: $[a_{\kappa}]=\frac{[\hbar]^{2}}{[m][\kappa]}=\frac{(\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}})^{2}}{\mathrm{kg}\cdot\mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}}}=\mathrm m$; $[\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{\hbar^{2}}]=\frac{\mathrm{kg}\cdot(\mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}})^{2}}{(\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}})^{2}}=\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-2}}=\mathrm J$; $[\frac{\hbar}{m\alpha c}]=\frac{\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}}}{\mathrm{kg}\cdot 1\cdot\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}}=\mathrm m$; and $[\alpha]=\frac{[\kappa]}{[\hbar][c]}=\frac{\mathrm{kg\,m^{3}\,s^{-2}}}{\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-1}}\cdot\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}}=1$. Hence the identities of (a) and (b) are dimensionally consistent, which is (d).

[Threshold and assembly] By [L2] the bottom of the continuous spectrum of the total operator is $-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=\mathcal E_{1}$, and the relative ground energy is a threshold and not an eigenvalue of the total operator, which is (e). Steps 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4 give (a)-(d); no numerical value of any parameter was used, so the example is conditional as recorded.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis used by the change-of-variables lemma cited below. For every real
$\lambda>0$ and every integer $k\ge0$ the function $r\mapsto r^{k}e^{-\lambda
r}$ is Lebesgue integrable on $(0,\infty)$ and

$$\int_0^\infty r^{k}e^{-\lambda r}\,dr=\frac{k!}{\lambda^{k+1}}.$$

The assertion is an identity for the Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative Borel
function; no probabilistic interpretation and no normalised density are
asserted. In particular no statement is made about any other exponent, about
complex $\lambda$, or about negative powers.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, $l\ge0$,
$k>0$, let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]], write
$$j:=\frac{\gamma}{2k}-l-1,$$
and for $a=2l+1$ and $n\in\mathbb N_0$ let
$$L_n^{(a)}(x):=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i\binom{n+a}{n-i}\frac{x^i}{i!}$$
be the $n$-th Laguerre polynomial of order $a$. Then:

(a) *substitution.* A $C^2$ function $u$ on $(0,\infty)$ satisfies $-u''+(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r)u=-k^2u$ if and only if $v(x):=e^{x/2}x^{-(l+1)}u(x/2k)$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $(0,\infty)$;

(b) *regular series.* With $v_0:=1$ and
$$v_{i+1}:=\frac{(i-j)v_i}{(i+1)(i+2l+2)}\qquad(i\ge0),$$
the power series $v(x):=\sum_{i\ge0}v_ix^i$ converges for every $x\in\mathbb R$ and defines a solution of $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) *regular solution and general solution.* The function
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r):=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$$
is a $C^\infty$ solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ with $u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ as $r\downarrow0$; it is, up to a nonzero scalar multiple, the only solution with $u(r)/r^{l+1}$ bounded as $r\downarrow0$; every solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ is $c_1u_{\mathrm{reg}}+c_2u_2$ with $u_2$ defined near zero by $u_2(r):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)\int_{r_*}^r u_{\mathrm{reg}}(s)^{-2}ds$, where $0<r_*<\delta$ and $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has no zero in $(0,\delta)$, and extended uniquely to $(0,\infty)$ by the regular initial-value equation, and every solution that is not a multiple of $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has $|u(r)|/r$ unbounded as $r\downarrow0$;

(d) *termination.* $v$ is a polynomial if and only if $j\in\mathbb N_0$; in that case $v$ is a nonzero constant multiple of $L_j^{(2l+1)}$, and
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=c\,r^{l+1}e^{-kr}L_j^{(2l+1)}(2kr)\quad(c\ne0)$$
lies in $L^2(0,\infty;dr)$;

(e) *eigenfunction.* If $j\in\mathbb N_0$ then $u_{\mathrm{reg}}\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu_{\mathrm{reg}}=-k^2u_{\mathrm{reg}}$; equivalently, for every $m$ the transported function $\psi(r\Omega):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $H^2(\mathbb R^3)\cap D(C)$ and satisfies $C\psi=-k^2\psi$.

The assertions are statements about the ordinary differential equation and
the operators $A_l,C$; no physical interpretation of $\gamma,k$ or of any
spectral level is made.

Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2 and P5, the readings of the declared
one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$, $\kappa>0$ and length scale
$a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, the energy-observable reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]], the bound-state data
of [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]], and the
spin-zero position law
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For each label let $\psi_{nlm}$ and
$\Psi_{nlm}=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$ be the bound vectors of the cited
theorem, and write $u_{nl}$ for the reduced regular solution with
$\psi_{nlm}(x)=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$. Then:

(a) for every label and every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ the position
outcome law in the unit preparation $[\Psi_{nlm}]$ is
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\|\psi_{nlm}\|^{-2}\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\Bigl(\int_{S^{2}}\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)\,|Y_{lm}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr)dr;$$
in particular, for a **radial** set $B=\{x:a<|x|<b\}$ with
$0\le a<b\le+\infty$ one has
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\frac{1}{\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}}\int_{a}^{b}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\,dr,$$
so the **radial density** $p_{nl}(r):=|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}/\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}$ is a
probability density on $(0,\infty)$: $p_{nl}\ge0$ and
$\int_{0}^{\infty}p_{nl}(r)\,dr=1$;

(b) for $n=1,l=m=0$ the normalized vector $\Psi_{100}$ has a representative
of the form
$$\Psi_{100}(x)=\zeta_{100}(\pi a_{\kappa}^{3})^{-1/2}e^{-r/a_{\kappa}},\qquad |\zeta_{100}|=1,$$
and its radial density is
$$p_{10}(r)=4r^{2}a_{\kappa}^{-3}e^{-2r/a_{\kappa}};$$
the mean of $p_{10}$ is $\int_{0}^{\infty}r\,p_{10}(r)\,dr=3a_{\kappa}/2$, the
unique maximum of $p_{10}$ is at $r=a_{\kappa}$, the spatial density
of this representative is $|\Psi_{100}|^{2}=\frac{1}{\pi a_{\kappa}^{3}}e^{-2r/a_{\kappa}}$,
strictly decreasing in $r$ and maximal at the origin,
and for every $\varepsilon>0$
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{100}}\bigl(\{|x|<\varepsilon\}\bigr)=\frac{1}{6}\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_{\kappa}}\Bigr)^{3}+O\Bigl(\bigl(\frac{\varepsilon}{a_{\kappa}}\bigr)^{4}\Bigr)>0,$$
which tends to $0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$: the density maximum at the
origin is not an atom of probability at any point;

(c) for every label the reduced solution has the polynomial-exponential form
$$u_{nl}(r)=c_{nl}\,r^{l+1}e^{-r/(na_{\kappa})}L_{n-l-1}^{(2l+1)}\bigl(2r/(na_{\kappa})\bigr)\qquad(c_{nl}\ne0),$$
with $L_{j}^{(a)}$ the Laguerre polynomial of integer order, so the radial
density of the level $(n,l)$ is a polynomial times $r^{2l+2}$ times a
decreasing exponential, and its normalisation constant is fixed by
$\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}|^{2}dr=\|\psi_{nlm}\|^{2}$;

(d) *Reading and scope.* The statements are conditional on P1, P2, P5, the
declared Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The radial density is the
reading of the model's position observable on radial sets; it is not a
trajectory, an orbit or a definite distance, and the model assigns positive
probability to every open ball around the origin and to arbitrarily large
radii. No measured radius, no measured density and no identification of
$a_{\kappa}$ with a laboratory length is asserted; numerical comparison
requires the measured constants as qualified empirical inputs and is deferred.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its
scalar law is the model's Born position law,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(d) for every unitary $V\in U(r)$, with $V_{\times}$ the matrix action of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clause (b),
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi},\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi};$$

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$. The real outcome spaces remain $\mathbb R$;
zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value
eigenstate. Finite-resolution records use the displayed Borel bin probabilities.

derivations.claim: [Closed forms] For $n=1$, $l=0$: $j=0$, $k=1/(na)=1/a$, so [L2] gives $u_{10}(r)=c\,r e^{-r/a}$. For $n=2$, $l=0$: $j=1$, $L_{1}^{(1)}(x)=2-x$ and $k=1/(2a)$, so $u_{20}(r)=c\,r e^{-r/(2a)}(2-r/a)$. For $n=2$, $l=1$: $j=0$, $L_{0}^{(3)}=1$ and $k=1/(2a)$, so $u_{21}(r)=c\,r^{2}e^{-r/(2a)}$. The constants $c$ are fixed by the normalisation condition $\|u_{nl}\|_{2}=1$, evaluated in the next step, giving the displayed coefficients of (a).

[Moments of the ground state] With $p_{10}=4a^{-3}r^{2}e^{-2r/a}$, [L1] gives $\int_0^\infty r\,p_{10}(r)dr=4a^{-3}\cdot3!/(2/a)^4=4a^{-3}\cdot6a^4/16=3a/2$ and $\int_0^\infty r^2p_{10}(r)dr=4a^{-3}\cdot4!/(2/a)^5=4a^{-3}\cdot24a^5/32=3a^2$. Thus the variance is $3a^2-(3a/2)^2=3a^2/4$.

[Cross-checks and scope] Since $R_{nl}=u_{nl}/r$, step 1.1 gives $R_{10}=2a^{-3/2}e^{-r/a}$, $R_{20}=2^{-3/2}a^{-3/2}(2-r/a)e^{-r/(2a)}$ and $R_{21}=2^{-3/2}3^{-1/2}a^{-3/2}(r/a)e^{-r/(2a)}$, which agree with the cited tabulated radial functions, and the value $5a$ of step 2.3 agrees with the circular-orbit formula $\langle r\rangle_{n,n-1}=n(n+\tfrac12)a$ at $n=2$; this is (e). Only the declared model, the cited mathematics and the exponential-moments lemma were used, and $a$ remains a model scale, so the scope statement (f) holds.
